messages:
maria: quick heads up — saw a regression on multi-tenant p95 after yesterday's kernel selection tweak. not huge, but long-seq tenants seeing 30-40ms extra latency when short-seq traffic spikes.
aj: yikes. which kernel change?
maria: the new fused-attn path for int8 that reduces per-token cost but increased per-batch setup time. wins for large contiguous batches but hurts when lots of small mini-batches form.
sasha: can you paste the profiler snapshot?
maria: pasted below — short version: when batch_size <= 4, setup overhead dominates. p95 short-seq latency went from 68ms -> ~100ms. overall token throughput still fine.
```
# snapshot from perf-run-1796
route: model-x (int8-fused)
input_dist: 60% short (<32), 40% long (512)
mini_batch_stats:
  avg_size: 6
  p95_size: 12
kernel_setup_ms: 8-12 (per mini-batch)
kv-hit-rate: 0.32 (shorts benefit less)
p95_latency_before: 68ms
p95_latency_after: 100ms
```
ryan: so the fused kernel has higher fixed setup but better amortization. this is classic batching fairness problem: long/short sequences + tenants compete for batch slots and tokens.
tanvi: agree. our current continuous-batcher uses token-credit buckets per-tenant but credits are static targets (e.g., 256 tokens/tenant). short-seq tenants burn through credits quickly then get deprioritized, which paradoxically increases latency for their tiny requests because they can't join forming batches.
aj: i've been thinking about a "latency equalizer" heuristic — give short-seq requests higher short-term priority by using a mini-batch credit pool that is separate from the normal token budget. basic idea: two buckets per tenant: short_credit and long_credit. short_credit refills faster but has a hard cap (e.g., 4-8 requests).
sasha: sketch config suggestion?
aj: sure, pseudo-config we tried locally:
```
continuous_batcher:
  min_batch_ms: 6
  max_wait_ms: 60
  token_budget_target: 512
  tenant_pools:
    default:
      short_credit_cap: 8
      short_refill_ms: 200
      long_credit_cap: 1024
      long_refill_ms: 2000
  mini_batch_threshold: 4
  credit_decay: 0.9  # aging to prevent starvation
```

maria: we ran a quick sim with this and saw short p95 drop back to ~72ms while long-seq p99 increased by ~5-8ms but throughput unchanged.
ryan: reasonable tradeoff. we should also consider kernel-aware routing: if the scheduler detects many minis (<4) forming, route those to int8-generic kernel that has lower setup but slightly higher per-token cost. switch back when contiguous batch size grows.
tanvi: kernel-aware routing + dual-credit pools seems promising. need to watch for tenant starvation: long tenants could be penalized under sustained short bursts. add proportional fairness weight so long tenants get min-share.
sasha: can we do a simple experiment in staging? plan: 1) enable dual-credit batcher with short_credit_cap=6, short_refill_ms=150; 2) add kernel fallback rule: if predicted batch_size < 5 use generic kernel; 3) run 30min mixed workload sim; collect p50/p95/p99 per-tenant and per-seq-length.
aj: I'll spin up a canary with traffic-gen. infra-bot: started job perf-sim-179612 on staging-3 (link: https://ci.internal/perf-sim-179612).
infra-bot: perf collector engaged, will post artifacts to /artifacts/perf-sim-179612.tar.gz when done.
maria: thanks. one more thought — KV cache effects: short requests tend to miss more because they're often new prefixes; consider providing preferential KV prefetching for tenants with many short requests (costy but might improve end-to-end latency).
ryan: note on metrics: add metric for "mini_batch_setup_ms" and "kernel_switch_count" so we can see if routing flips are thrashing. also log tenant_credit_balance histogram.
tanvi: +1. i'd also add an SLA guard: if any tenant's p99 exceeds SLA threshold, reduce short_credit aggressiveness automatically until p99 recovers.
sasha: ok sounds actionable. aj, can you own the canary run? maria, collect the traces and put a short writeup with graphs. we'll sync tomorrow at 10am to decide rollout. :thumbsup:
aj: on it — starting traffic-gen now. expected artifacts ~40m after run.
maria: will pull traces and post a short summary to this thread. thanks all. :coffee:
